agree.reason: The letter is clear and candid, but a skeptical HR manager would read a teacher who admits having no GMP or records experience and offers no proof of documentation discipline, so it probably doesn't get a phone screen.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'cut training in half' claim and states the gaps plainly, though 'most of them are teenagers using acids, open flames and glassware for the first time' adds a little colour the facts don't give.

works_the_facts.reason: It leaves out the strongest numbers available: the cut from 20 to 12 hours of new-teacher training (40% shorter), the signed training records, and the two clean state audits. It also doesn't turn the pass-rate rise into its stronger form, a 17-point gain.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after for training (20 hours down to 12) is the honest substitute for the 'half' claim and is never mentioned, so the reader gets nothing to set against the 12 hours.

qualification.reason: The only hedge, 'shorten training where possible', is vague, and the letter leaves out the checkable conditions: the GMP course ending May 2, the earliest start date of June 14, and interview availability.

objections.reason: It raises the records and regulation objection itself, then answers it with a vague habit instead of the facts that would settle it (signed records for every trainee and quiz, two state audits with no findings, GMP course enrolment).

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter as asked, but it keeps placeholders for her name, the company and the manager even though Laura Benitez, Calder Pharmaceuticals in Westfield and Karen Doyle were known.
